working_title: Dunstanburgh Castle: England's Best-Value Links You've Probably Overlooked
angle: Dunstanburgh Castle Golf Club has just entered the England Top 100 for the first time (ranked No. 99 in the 2026 edition) at a green fee that sits comfortably under £60, making it arguably the shrewdest value play in English links golf right now. The post pitches it as a genuine bucket-list add-on for anyone already planning a Northumberland or East Lothian trip, not a consolation-prize course.
research_notes:
- Dunstanburgh Castle Golf Club is located on the Northumberland Heritage Coast at Embleton Bay, Alnwick NE66 3XQ. Course wraps around Embleton Bay with views across the North Sea.
- Entered the England Top 100 (top100golfcourses.com) for the first time in the 2026 edition at No. 99, described as 'a spectacular coastal links in Northumberland into national recognition' (source: top100golfcourses.com).
- Also listed on the NCG Top 100s: England list; one of only two north-east England courses on that list, alongside Goswick Links around 25 miles up the coast (source: nationalclubgolfer.com).
- Designed by James Braid (five-time Open Champion) in 1922; the layout has remained largely unchanged for over a century. Club traces roots to 1900. A further update by architect Jonathan Gaunt was carried out in 2016 (source: golfempire.co.uk).
- Green fee listed at £55 in the top100golfcourses.com 2026 data, ranking it among nine England Top 100 courses playable for under £75. Golfshake lists midweek guide rate of £26/round and £32/day; weekend £30/round, £38/day — these figures may be outdated or refer to a concessionary rate, so treat with caution and describe value in general terms rather than quoting specific figures.
- Set within an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty; course plays in the shadow of 14th-century Dunstanburgh Castle ruins. Castle ruins form the backdrop to the 13th green (source: 2fore1.co.uk).
- No driving range on site due to the tightness of the coastal land; short-game area and putting green by the 1st tee (source: nationalclubgolfer.com).
- Routing note: returns to clubhouse after 6 holes before looping out for the final 12 (similar in concept to Western Gailes) (source: nationalclubgolfer.com).
- Walk from 1st green to 2nd tee involves a steep climb of around 60 feet — worth flagging as a practical visitor tip.
- Visitors welcome throughout the year; Sunday mornings until 10:30am reserved for club competitions. Buggies available but must be pre-booked (source: dunstanburgh.com).
- No driving range — useful practical note for a visitor who wants a warm-up.
- Situated 40 miles north of Newcastle, 35 miles south of the Scottish border; positioned as a natural stopover between England's north-east and East Lothian (source: nationalclubgolfer.com / dunstanburgh.com).
- Northumberland coast has 8 links or downland courses in total, all open to visitors (source: northumberlandsgolfcoast.com). Others nearby include Goswick Links, Bamburgh Castle, Alnmouth, Seahouses, Magdalene Fields.
- Post should NOT duplicate the East Lothian guide already published (scotland-s-golf-coast...) — frame Northumberland as a distinct destination, perhaps as the English side of a cross-border links trip.
- Membership currently closed with a waiting list (source: dunstanburgh.com) — a subtle signal of the course's growing reputation worth a brief mention.
